messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: routing.tail_p99 spikes in eu-west-1 > 3000ms for 5m. Impact: streaming stalls and degraded throughput. Alert details: https://dash.redwood/alerts/1739995555

Eric (oncall): saw this - paging team. I'm jumping in.

Alice: confirmed. p95 up ~800ms, p99 ~3.2s for router->model path, streaming stalls reported by a couple of partners.

Ben: any config rollouts recently? I can check deployments.

Caroline: there was a routing-policy rollout this morning (affinity-v2). Canary looked fine in us-east but not eu-west.

Dave: logs show a tight concentration to shard-42 behind lb-euw2-03. Hot partitioning.

Eric (oncall): ok immediate priority: 1) mitigate customer impact 2) identify root cause 3) avoid noisy rollback if possible. I'll coordinate live.

SRE rotations: tagging oncall infra as well. @Kevin can you look at loadbalancer sharding map?

Kevin: looking. initial hypothesis: affinity-v2 changed seed mixing -> some flows got pinned to a few routers. I see hash distribution skewed: bucket 42 ~62% of traffic for certain routing key prefixes.

Ben: copying routing policy snippet from the rollout:

```
policy: affinity-v2
seed: fnv1a_mod(1024)
weights:
  default: 1.0
  regional_bias: { eu-west-1: 1.2 }
```

Alice: that regional_bias line plus the new seed could produce local hotness. Might be bias *and* seed collision.

Eric (oncall): mitigation options: A) revert affinity-v2 rollout B) adjust weights to reduce eu-west bias C) add ephemeral routing fallback to round-robin for streaming requests. Thoughts?

Caroline: reverting will take ~10m and affects canary -> prod progression. We might revert canary only for eu-west, but the rollout was global config.

Dave: adding fallback sounds safer. We have a runtime flag to force round-robin for streaming route 'stream.v1'. I can flip it in eu-west and monitor.

Kevin: while you flip, I'll push a temporary mapping update to de-opt bucket 42 via weight override: set weight(bucket42)=0.6. That should rebalance.

Eric (oncall): do it. Please post commands you run.

Dave: running:
```
# runtime toggle
curl -X POST "https://config-api.internal/switches" -d '{"key":"stream.v1.force_rr","region":"eu-west-1","value":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

Dave: toggle applied.

Kevin: applying weight override for bucket 42:
```
./rb ctl set-weight --region eu-west-1 --bucket 42 --weight 0.6 --reason "mitigate hot partition"
```

Kevin: applied. propagation ~30s.

Alice: seeing initial drop in p99 from 3200ms -> ~1400ms within 90s. p95 now ~420ms. Streaming stalls count dropping.

Ben: confirmed logs: request fanout to lb-euw2-03 decreased 72% -> 28% of stream.v1. Good.

Caroline: still seeing some tails for long-hold streaming sessions ( >60s). Might be queued connections on a few nodes. I'm going to cordon lb-euw2-03 for rolling restart.

Eric (oncall): go ahead, but drain before restart. Post the drain command.

Caroline: draining:
```
# drain
./infra drain-node lb-euw2-03 --grace-period 60
# restart
./infra reboot-node lb-euw2-03
```

Caroline: node restarted and back in service. p99 trending down to ~700ms.

SRE rotations: thumbs. Any customer-visible incidents reported?

Alice: Support flagged two partners with streaming timeouts (Client IDs redacted), but they auto-retry and errors are within SLA window for non-streaming. We should notify them about temporary degradation.

Eric (oncall): I'll open an incident page and notify customer success. Incident declared: partial degraded streaming in eu-west-1, elevated latency p95/p99 between 1739995450-1739995700 (approx).

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0427. Pagerduty: https://pd.redwood/INC-2026-0427

Ben: root cause hypotheses: incorrect interaction between affinity-v2 seed function and regional_bias weight producing hash collisions -> hot partition, amplified by LB node unevenness. Need repro and fix.

Kevin: I can reproduce locally by running the seed with traffic fingerprint set to EU prefixes. The distribution shows >50% mapping to bucket 42 with new seed+bias.

Caroline: immediate next steps: 1) revert regional_bias or change seed algorithm 2) add more robust rollout checks (canary per-region distribution heatmap) 3) postmortem to capture detection gap.

Eric (oncall): agree. For now keep stream.v1 force_rr true in eu-west until a tested seed/weight patch is deployed. Set a TTL for the toggle to 6h.

Dave: setting TTL:
```
curl -X POST "https://config-api.internal/switches" -d '{"key":"stream.v1.force_rr","region":"eu-west-1","value":true,"ttl":21600}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

Dave: TTL set.

Alice: monitoring dashboards show stable p99 ~600-800ms for last 8m, streaming stall events dropped to baseline.

Caroline: filed bug: ROUTER-7654 "affinity-v2 seed/regional_bias causes bucket skew in eu-west" assigned to Ben.

Ben: I'll own the fix. Plan: run exhaustive hash stability tests, evaluate alternate mixing fn (murmur) and remove global regional_bias knob in favor of traffic-steering policy that uses consistent hashing with node capacity weighting. Estimate 48h for patch + test.

Eric (oncall): good. For the incident timeline: root alert at 1739995555, mitigations started 1739995600, observed improvement 1739995660, drain/restart done 1739995685, TTL enforcement done 1739995720, incident declared mitigated 1739995735.

SRE rotations: closing the page but keep monitoring for 2h. Postmortem owner: Ben. Customer comms: Eric + CS will draft an advisory.

Kevin: one more note: telemetry gap - alerting threshold was p99>3s for 5m. We got lucky that streaming health signals (stall counts) weren't in that alert. Recommend adding a streaming-stall alert tied to router queue depth.

Eric (oncall): agreed, file a follow-up.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0427 status: mitigated. Actions:
- Mitigation: force_rr toggle (eu-west) + weight override bucket 42 + restart lb-euw2-03
- RCA owner: Ben (ROUTER-7654)
- Postmortem ETA: 72h
- Customer comm owner: Eric (oncall)

Alice: thanks team. We'll loop back with CS and get a short advisory out.

Ben: starting repro + test plan now. Will post updates in the issue.

Eric (oncall): I'll close this Slack thread once postmortem doc link is up. Great quick work, folks. :thumbsup:
